audit: DataForge V3.1 — Phase 1A Baseline Reliability Audit
selection_rationale: Maximise diversity across repositories, languages and verifier failure mechanisms while ensuring DeepSeek is likely to produce a non-empty patch (so grading evidence exists). No two tasks share the same primary risk mechanism; each maps to one or more of the ten investigation hypotheses.

tasks.primary_hypothesis: H5 (runner crash/nonzero exit misread) + H3 (parser misidentification) + patch contamination
tasks.suspected_failure_mechanism: tests/run_script.sh wraps mocha in `timeout 120 ... || echo '{"tests":[],...}'`, so any crash/timeout/nonzero exit is replaced by an empty-but-valid JSON blob. tests/parser.py extracts JSON via non-greedy regex `({\n.*?\n})` and only reads `passes`/`pending`/`failures`. A 'before all' hook failure (suite init failure) is emitted under `failures` with no individual tests, so absence of the required tests is the only signal; a genuinely broken environment is indistinguishable from a failing agent. model.patch capture uses `git add -A` after npm install + redis-server, pulling in unrelated binaries (appendonlydir/*.rdb).
tasks.source_evidence: tests/run_script.sh lines with `|| echo`; tests/parser.py parse_test_output; tests/test_patch.patch; observed directly in pilot-deepseek-2
tasks.expected_diagnostic_signal: Verifier JSON shows `failures` containing only a 'before all' hook entry while required tests are absent; run-script-stdout contains an empty `{"tests":[]...}` appended after the real mocha JSON; model.patch contains non-source binary files.
tasks.verification_method: Oracle vs no-op controls; fresh-sandbox patch_replay of captured patch; parse run-script-stdout manually vs verifier output.json; inspect model.patch for non-source paths.
tasks.selection_justification: Only repository using mocha+redis with JSON reporter; already surfaced a real masked-hook-failure mechanism in the pilot, and is the clearest case of model.patch contamination. Cheap (~8 min) and highly deterministic to reproduce.

tasks.suspected_failure_mechanism: run_script.sh runs `go test -v -run "^(...)$" ./internal/server/auth || true`. The `|| true` guarantees exit code 0 regardless of compile failure, panic, or test timeout. tests/parser.py (regex `^\s*--- (PASS|FAIL|SKIP):\s+(\S+)\s+\(.*\)$`) only captures `--- PASS/FAIL/SKIP:` sub-test lines; a `go build` failure emits none, so a broken build is graded purely on missing tests. Exact-anchored `-run` regex (`^(${test_names})$`) means a required test whose name is a prefix of another would not match.
tasks.source_evidence: tests/run_script.sh `go test ... || true`; tests/parser.py regex line; config.json fail_to_pass list
tasks.expected_diagnostic_signal: Non-zero real `go test` exit code visible in run-script-stdout while verifier reward is derived only from parsed test names; a compile error line present with zero parsed matches.
tasks.verification_method: Oracle vs no-op controls; inject a deliberate compile break and confirm reward behaviour without changing the official task; compare parsed names to required names; patch_replay.
tasks.selection_justification: Repo with the most Go tasks (78) and a classic failure-masking `|| true` pattern (present in ALL 78). Sub-test-named duplicate identities (`par_gotest` bucket). Distinct from teleport/vuls/navidrome Go tasks by masking mechanism.

tasks.suspected_failure_mechanism: tests/parser.py does `cleaned_line.split()[2]` to extract the test route from `--- PASS/FAIL/SKIP/ERROR:` lines. This crashes (IndexError, uncaught -> parser produces no output.json -> reward 0) if a line lacks a third token, and misattributes names for Go subtests whose identifier contains a space. It also treats `--- ERROR:` as a valid status but Go emits `--- FAIL:` for panics, so ERROR handling is largely dead code. No `|| true` masking here, so failures DO propagate to exit code but the parser determines the reward.
tasks.source_evidence: tests/parser.py lines using `cleaned_line.split()[2]`; run_script.sh `go test -v -run ... 2>&1` (no `|| true`); config.json fail_to_pass list
tasks.expected_diagnostic_signal: Any `--- <STATUS>:` line with fewer than 3 whitespace tokens, or a test name with a space, alters the parsed set; parser IndexError on malformed lines.
tasks.verification_method: Fuzz the parser with synthetic `--- FAIL:` lines (with/without extra tokens); oracle vs no-op controls; compare raw vs parsed names; patch_replay.
tasks.selection_justification: Distinct from flipt: here masking is absent and the risk is parser fragility + ERROR semantics. 58 Go tasks share this parser family; f2p list has 67 entries (largest fail_to_pass set among candidates), exercising many identifiers.

tasks.suspected_failure_mechanism: tests/parser.py collects results across three regex passes (primary, summary, verbose) but `export_to_json` deduplicates by name using `{result.name: result for result in results}` — LAST occurrence wins, so a test appearing as PASSED in verbose output and FAILED in the summary resolves to whichever pass ran last. Its regexes require the literal `.py::` substring, so any required identifier without `.py::` (or with unusual parametrisation formatting) is silently dropped. Deterministic reward derived solely from parsed names.
tasks.source_evidence: tests/parser.py parse_test_output (three regexes) and export_to_json dedup dict; config.json uses 'scripts/tests/test_new_solr_updater.py::TestParseLog::...'
tasks.expected_diagnostic_signal: Duplicate names with conflicting statuses collapsing to one; required names containing characters outside `[^\s]+\.py::[^\s]+` being absent from output.json.
tasks.verification_method: Feed crafted stdout containing the same test in both PASSED and FAILED forms and observe final status; inspect raw pytest `-v --tb=short` output vs output.json; oracle vs no-op; patch_replay.
tasks.selection_justification: Only selected repo using this specific triple-regex + name-dedup parser (82 tasks). Small, self-contained test file (single module) so a full run is cheap and the parser behaviour is isolateable. Distinct from ansible's pytest parser.

tasks.suspected_failure_mechanism: run_script.sh runs `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -cover -json -race -shuffle on -tags pam -run "^(...)$" ./lib/asciitable`. `-shuffle on` randomises test order (with `-race`), so results can differ between runs; tests/parser.py parses the Go `-json` event stream, recording only `Action` in {pass,fail,skip}. It ignores `run`/`output`/`pause` events, and a package-level failure (panic) emits no per-test `Test` field, so a crashing required test can simply be absent rather than FAILED. parser's textual fallback only runs when the JSON parse produced zero results.
tasks.source_evidence: run_script.sh `-shuffle on -race -json`; tests/parser.py JSON loop `if 'Test' in data and 'Action' in data`; config.json required names TestFullTable/TestTruncatedTable/TestHeadlessTable
tasks.expected_diagnostic_signal: Same patch yielding different parsed sets across repeated runs; required test absent from output.json (not FAILED) after a panic; `-shuffle` seed differing between executions.
tasks.verification_method: Run the verifier multiple times on the same oracle patch and diff verdicts (repeat-run test for H6); inspect Go `-json` stream for panic/fail without Test field; oracle vs no-op; multiple patch_replay runs.
tasks.selection_justification: The only selected task whose verifier uses Go `-json` AND `-shuffle on`; directly targets reproducibility (H6), which no other selected task isolates. 68 teleport tasks share this class.

tasks.primary_hypothesis: H5 (`|| true` masking) + H1 (impossible-to-pass parametrised IDs)
tasks.suspected_failure_mechanism: run_selected_tests loops over files and runs `pytest -v "$test_path" --tb=short || true`; the literal `|| true` discards pytest's non-zero exit, so only the parser verdict matters. fail_to_pass contains parametrised identifiers like `test_methods[get-kwargs0]` and many pass_to_pass entries; tests/parser.py must reproduce these exact strings (including `::` and `[...]`) for the subset check `all_required <= passed_tests` to hold. The parser's regex (`[^\s]+\.py::[^\s]+`) cannot represent identifiers containing whitespace, which pytest parametrisation can introduce (`[get - kwargs0]`).
tasks.source_evidence: run_script.sh `pytest -v "$test_path" ... || true`; config.json fail_to_pass/test_methods[...] and pass_to_pass lists; tests/parser.py regex
tasks.expected_diagnostic_signal: A required identifier present in raw pytest output but not matched by the parser pattern (e.g. containing a space), producing a false FAIL; masked pytest exit code with zero parsed failures.
tasks.verification_method: Oracle vs no-op; inspect raw pytest `-v` lines for the required IDs vs output.json; synthetically test parser regex against parametrised names with spaces; patch_replay.
tasks.selection_justification: Repo with 82 tasks and the most parametrised test identifiers in the selected set; tests the H1/H2 direction (passing test reported failing) that openlibrary covers less. Distinct from openlibrary by pytest invocation shape (per-file loop + `|| true`).

tasks.primary_hypothesis: H3 (parser loses tests) + H2 (passing reported failing)
tasks.suspected_failure_mechanism: tests/parser.py identifies test cases ONLY by Unicode checkmarks (✓ ✔ for pass, ○ ✎ for skip, ✕ for fail) after stripping non-printable characters. jest run with `--verbose --silent` may not emit these glyphs under all reporters/TTY conditions; if the glyphs are absent or rendered as bytes that `isprintable()` rejects, every test is silently dropped and the whole task scores FAIL regardless of the code. The parser also splits `PASS/FAIL` file markers by whitespace and reconstructs names as `<file> | <suite> | <case>`, which must exactly equal the 39 fail_to_pass + 124 pass_to_pass identifiers. Large p2p surface (124) amplifies any single mis-parse.
tasks.source_evidence: run_script.sh `npx jest --verbose --silent --maxWorkers=1 --forceExit`; tests/parser.py CHECKMARKS_* constants and isprintable cleaning; config.json 39 fail_to_pass + 124 pass_to_pass
tasks.expected_diagnostic_signal: Non-empty jest output with zero parsed test cases (all glyphs stripped); required identifiers absent from output.json while present in raw jest text.
tasks.verification_method: Oracle vs no-op; inspect raw jest output for glyph presence vs output.json contents; craft output with glyphs removed and observe reward; patch_replay.
tasks.selection_justification: Only selected jest/TypeScript task; Unicode-checkmark parsing is a mechanism unique in the set and highly fragile. Largest pass_to_pass list among candidates (124) — best stress test for the subset check and name reconstruction.

replacement_policy: Freeze is final unless a task is proven impossible to execute; if so, the blocker and replacement justification are recorded in findings BEFORE examining outcome results.
